_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Angola covering Kongo Kingdom, Ndongo/Mbundu (Queen Njinga), Portuguese colonisation (oldest in sub-Saharan Africa 1575–1975), Atlantic slave trade centre, liberation movements (MPLA/FNLA/UNITA), civil war 1975–2002 (Cold War proxy), dos Santos era, oil wealth, and Lourenço reforms.

ethnic_groups.name: Ovimbundu
ethnic_groups.notes: Largest ethnic group; concentrated in central highlands; Umbundu language; historically associated with UNITA

ethnic_groups.name: Mbundu/Ambundu
ethnic_groups.notes: Concentrated around Luanda and Malanje; Kimbundu language; historically associated with MPLA

ethnic_groups.name: Bakongo
ethnic_groups.notes: Northern Angola and Cabinda; Kikongo language; part of historic Kingdom of Kongo; FNLA base

ethnic_groups.name: Lunda-Chokwe
ethnic_groups.notes: Eastern Angola; historically linked to Lunda Empire; diamond mining regions

ethnic_groups.name: Ngangela
ethnic_groups.notes: Eastern Angola; multiple sub-groups including Luchazi, Mbunda, Nyemba

ethnic_groups.name: Nyaneka-Humbe
ethnic_groups.notes: Southern Angola; pastoralists in Huíla province

ethnic_groups.name: Kwanyama/Ovambo
ethnic_groups.notes: Far southern Angola; related to Namibian Ovambo; border straddling community

ethnic_groups.name: San/Bushmen
ethnic_groups.notes: Small hunter-gatherer communities in southern Angola

ethnic_groups.name: Mestiço (Mixed)
ethnic_groups.notes: Portuguese-African mixed heritage; historically influential in Luanda creole society

natural_resources.notes: Sub-Saharan Africa's second-largest oil producer (1.2M bpd); Catoca diamond mine world's 4th largest; extreme resource curse—oil wealth concentrated in elite hands while 54% live in poverty; deepwater offshore fields (Block 17/18); LNG plant at Soyo
natural_resources.resource_curse_risk: High (oil dependency >90% of exports; 'Futungo' elite capture)

military.notes: Battle-hardened from 27-year civil war; Cuban troops deployed 1975-91 (peak 55k); intervened in DRC (both Congo wars); South African apartheid forces opposed MPLA; Cold War proxy battlefield

submarine_cables: SACS (South Atlantic Cable System, to Brazil)
infrastructure.notes: SACS cable connects Angola directly to Brazil; Lobito Corridor railway revitalisation; Luanda expressway; critical infrastructure still war-damaged.

climate_environment.notes: Giant sable antelope (national symbol, endemic, critically endangered); Okavango River source; mangrove forests along coast; charcoal deforestation.

debt_aid.notes: Chinese oil-backed loans ~$25B; Isabel dos Santos scandal ($3.7B alleged embezzlement); Lourenço anti-corruption drive post-2017

education.notes: Civil war destroyed education infrastructure; Portuguese-language instruction; severe teacher shortage; 30% of children out of school; gender gap significant in rural areas

diaspora_migration.notes: DRC refugees hosted; Chinese workers ~260k (infrastructure projects); retornados (Portuguese settlers who left 1975, ~300k); significant student diaspora in Portugal/Brazil
diaspora_migration.immigration_policy: Moderate; work permits for Chinese/Portuguese workers

digital_economy.notes: Among most expensive internet in Africa; submarine cable (SACS to Brazil) improved connectivity; Unitel dominant mobile operator; oil dependence limits tech diversification; fintech growing

country_profile.notes_unique: Sub-Saharan Africa's second-largest oil producer; endured a 27-year civil war (1975–2002) between MPLA and UNITA that shaped Cold War proxy dynamics in Africa.

geography.terrain: Narrow coastal plain; vast interior plateau (1000-2000m); tropical rainforest in north (Cabinda); semi-arid in south
geography.notes: Cabinda province is an exclave separated by DR Congo; Kwanza River is longest wholly within Angola; Okavango Delta fed by rivers from Angolan highlands.

economy_extended.notes: Oil-dependent (90%+ of exports); Sonangol national oil company; IMF programme 2018-21; kwanza devaluation; diversification efforts; Lobito Corridor rail project (US/EU funded).

health.notes: Severe healthcare worker shortage; urban-rural gap extreme; malaria #1 killer; yellow fever vaccination required; post-civil war healthcare infrastructure still recovering.

food_agriculture.notes: Massive agricultural potential (pre-war was coffee exporter); landmines still obstruct farming; cassava staple food; Chinese and Brazilian agricultural partnerships.

energy.notes: Africa's 2nd-largest oil producer; OPEC member; Laúca hydropower dam (2070MW); Caculo Cabaça dam under construction (2172MW); massive rural electrification gap; LNG plant (Soyo).

transport.notes: New Luanda International Airport (NAIL/Dr António Agostinho Neto) opened; Lobito Corridor railway rehabilitation (Benguela Railway to DRC/Zambia); road infrastructure heavily damaged by civil war.

tourism.notes: Tourism largely undeveloped; high costs (Luanda among world's most expensive cities); visa-on-arrival introduced; ecotourism potential in national parks; civil war legacy constrains infrastructure.

human_rights_gender.notes: MPLA single-party dominance; LGBTQ+ decriminalised in 2021 penal code; high child labour in agriculture; Isabel dos Santos corruption scandal; limited press freedom.

security_stability.notes: Post-civil war stability (2002 ceasefire); Cabinda FLEC separatism largely dormant; security forces credibly accused of extra-judicial killings in Lunda; landmines remain (~60,000+ still buried).

cultural_heritage.national_dish: Muamba de galinha (chicken palm oil stew)
cultural_heritage.media_landscape: State-controlled TV/radio (TPA, RNA); private newspapers; internet access growing; press freedom limited
cultural_heritage.notes: Kizomba dance/music originated in Luanda; Kuduro music global influence; strong oral tradition; Mbanza-Kongo capital of ancient Kongo Kingdom; carnival tradition.

legal_system.customary_law_role: Recognised for local matters in rural areas
legal_system.notes: 2010 constitution established presidential republic; Supreme Court; Constitutional Court; customary courts in rural areas; slow judicial reform.

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global.
comparative_rankings.notes: Africa's 2nd-largest oil producer; vast underutilised agricultural potential.

current_leader.name: João Lourenço
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: Elected in 2017; re-elected 2022; anti-corruption agenda targeting dos Santos era

former_leaders.name: Agostinho Neto
former_leaders.notes: First president; MPLA leader; poet and independence hero; died in office in Moscow

former_leaders.name: José Eduardo dos Santos
former_leaders.notes: 38-year rule; longest-serving African leader at time; civil war to oil boom; died 2022 in Spain

910.name: Early Inhabitants and Stone Age Angola
910.description: Stone Age occupation of Angola; San/Khoisan hunter-gatherers in the south; earliest Bantu migration begins.

sub_clusters.name: Stone Age Populations
sub_clusters.description: Archaeological sites across Angola show Early, Middle, and Late Stone Age occupation; rock shelters in the central highlands; Khoisan hunter-gatherers in southern Angola.

sub_clusters.name: Early Bantu Migration into Angola
sub_clusters.description: Bantu-speaking peoples begin migrating from the Cameroon-Nigeria borderlands through the Congo Basin into Angola; introduction of iron-working, pottery, and agriculture.

920.name: Kingdom of Kongo
920.description: The Kingdom of Kongo, one of Africa's most powerful states, dominates the region with its capital at Mbanza Kongo; early contact and conversion to Christianity through Portugal.

sub_clusters.name: Foundation and Expansion of Kongo
sub_clusters.description: Lukeni lua Nimi founds the Kongo Kingdom c.1390; capital at Mbanza Kongo; federation of provinces (Mbata, Soyo, Mpangu, Mbamba, Nsundi); agriculture, trade, and raffia cloth currency.

sub_clusters.name: Kongo-Portuguese Contact and Christianity
sub_clusters.description: Diogo Cão reaches Kongo 1483; Manikongo Nzinga a Nkuwu baptised as João I 1491; his son Afonso I (Mvemba a Nzinga) embraces Christianity and literacy; diplomatic exchanges with Vatican and Lisbon.

sub_clusters.name: Kongo Kingdom Decline
sub_clusters.description: Slave trade undermines royal authority; Battle of Mbwila 1665 (Portuguese defeat Kongo, kill King António I); kingdom fragments into warring factions; Kimpa Vita's Antonian movement 1704.

930.name: Kingdom of Ndongo and Queen Njinga
930.description: The Mbundu Kingdom of Ndongo resists Portuguese colonisation; Queen Njinga (Ana de Sousa Nzinga Mbande) becomes one of Africa's most celebrated resistance leaders.

sub_clusters.name: Kingdom of Ndongo
sub_clusters.description: Mbundu kingdom of Ndongo ruled by the ngola (king, from which 'Angola' derives); iron-working; resistance to Portuguese slave raids and fortification at Luanda.

sub_clusters.name: Queen Njinga's Resistance
sub_clusters.description: Njinga becomes queen of Ndongo 1624; legendary negotiation with Portuguese governor (chair incident); allies with Dutch against Portugal; conquers Matamba; fights for decades; makes peace 1657.

sub_clusters.name: Portuguese Foundation of Luanda
sub_clusters.description: Paulo Dias de Novais founds São Paulo de Luanda 1575 — oldest European-founded city in sub-Saharan Africa; becomes primary slave-trading port; Portuguese penetration into interior.

930.name: Angola and the Atlantic Slave Trade
930.description: Angola becomes the single largest source of enslaved Africans for the Atlantic slave trade; an estimated 5.7 million people are shipped from Angolan ports, primarily to Brazil.

sub_clusters.name: Slave Trade Expansion
sub_clusters.description: Portuguese slavers (pombeiros) penetrate interior; Luanda and Benguela as major embarkation ports; wars of enslavement; presídios (forts) along trade routes.

sub_clusters.name: Angola-Brazil Slave Trade Axis
sub_clusters.description: Direct Angola-Brazil trade route dominates the South Atlantic; Brazilian cachaça, tobacco, and textiles exchanged for enslaved peoples; cultural connections persist; trade continues illegally after 1836 ban.

940.name: Portuguese Colonial Rule
940.description: Portugal consolidates colonial control after abolition of slave trade; forced labour (contrato), plantation economy, and racial hierarchy; longest European colonisation in sub-Saharan Africa.

sub_clusters.name: Colonial Consolidation and Pacification Wars
sub_clusters.description: Portugal's 'pacification campaigns' against Ovimbundu, Kwanyama, and Dembos peoples; Berlin Conference confirms Portuguese claims; Angola's borders fixed by treaties with Britain and Germany.

sub_clusters.name: Forced Labour and Contract System
sub_clusters.description: Abolition of slavery replaced by contrato (contract) forced labour; cotton, coffee, and sisal plantations; indígena/assimilado racial classification; Henrique Galvão's damning 1947 report.

sub_clusters.name: Colonial Coffee Economy and White Settlement
sub_clusters.description: Angola becomes world's fourth-largest coffee producer; Salazar's Estado Novo encourages Portuguese settlement; settler population rises from 44,000 (1940) to 340,000 (1974).

950.name: Liberation Movements and Independence War
950.description: Three rival liberation movements — MPLA, FNLA, and UNITA — wage a 14-year war against Portuguese colonial rule; Carnation Revolution in Lisbon precipitates independence.

sub_clusters.name: Formation of Liberation Movements
sub_clusters.description: MPLA (Agostinho Neto, 1956); FNLA (Holden Roberto, 1962); UNITA (Jonas Savimbi, 1966); ethnic and ideological divides: MPLA (Mbundu/Luanda creoles/Marxist), FNLA (Bakongo), UNITA (Ovimbundu).

sub_clusters.name: Angolan War of Independence
sub_clusters.description: Luanda prison attack and Baixa de Cassange cotton revolt (4 February 1961); UPA/FNLA massacre in northern Angola; Portuguese counter-insurgency; war drains Portugal.

sub_clusters.name: Independence and Immediate Civil War
sub_clusters.description: Carnation Revolution in Lisbon April 1974; Alvor Accords January 1975; transitional government collapses; MPLA takes Luanda; independence 11 November 1975; South African invasion; Cuban intervention; FNLA defeated.

960.name: Angolan Civil War (1975–2002)
960.description: One of Africa's longest and deadliest civil wars; Cold War proxy conflict between Soviet/Cuban-backed MPLA and US/South African-backed UNITA; devastation of infrastructure and millions displaced.

sub_clusters.name: Cold War Proxy Phase
sub_clusters.description: Soviet arms and Cuban troops support MPLA; US CIA and South African military back UNITA/FNLA; Cuito Cuanavale battle 1988; New York Accords link Namibian independence to Cuban withdrawal.

sub_clusters.name: Failed Peace and Resumed War
sub_clusters.description: Bicesse Accords 1991; elections 1992 (MPLA wins, Savimbi rejects results); war resumes; Lusaka Protocol 1994; diamond-fueled UNITA insurgency; siege of Huambo and Kuito; Savimbi killed February 2002; ceasefire.

960.name: Dos Santos Era and Oil State
960.description: José Eduardo dos Santos rules for 38 years; Angola becomes Africa's second-largest oil producer; Sonangol and Futungo elite amass enormous wealth amid mass poverty.

sub_clusters.name: Dos Santos Presidency
sub_clusters.description: Dos Santos succeeds Neto 1979; MPLA transitions from Marxism to market economy 1990s; constitutional changes consolidate power; daughter Isabel dos Santos becomes Africa's richest woman.

sub_clusters.name: Oil Wealth and Resource Curse
sub_clusters.description: Oil revenues soar (peak $60 billion+ annually); Luanda becomes world's most expensive city; extreme inequality; 'Angolagate' corruption scandal; missing $32 billion IMF query.

960.name: Lourenço Era and Reform Agenda
960.description: João Lourenço succeeds dos Santos; anti-corruption campaign targets dos Santos family; economic diversification efforts; demographic youth bulge and unemployment.

sub_clusters.name: Lourenço Anti-Corruption Drive
sub_clusters.description: Lourenço removes dos Santos loyalists; Isabel dos Santos charged with fraud; Generals Kopelipa and Dino arrested; Sonangol restructured; international asset freezes.

sub_clusters.name: Economic Diversification Challenges
sub_clusters.description: Oil price crash and COVID-19 hammer economy; privatisation programme (ProPriv); agriculture and mining diversification; IMF programme; 60% of population under 25 faces unemployment.

sub_clusters.name: Angola's Regional Diplomacy
sub_clusters.description: Lourenço mediates DRC-Rwanda tensions; Angola brokers Great Lakes peace efforts; Atlantic coast LNG projects; growing role in African Union diplomacy.
